_doc: THE ONE DECLARATION of cloud-code's bottom navigation (#562). tabs.js builds the bar from this list in this order and nothing else restates it: the tester (test/test-cloud-nav.sh) renders the bar through the same tabs.js and reads the order back off the rendered model. `view` selects the renderer in index.js::VIEWS; `icon` is a class of Acode's own icon font (src/res/icons/style.css) and the tester proves each one exists there. The Editor tab is Acode itself (Chat replaced Home: every Home tile was a duplicate of a tab, and its Configs card moved to the top-right Profile & Config page), untouched: selecting it hides every cloud panel and nothing else.

nav._doc: Measured fit (#562): seven tabs is more than any fleet nav. At 360 px CSS width (the narrowest phone the owner's fleet targets) a tab is 51.4 px wide, above the 48 px touch floor, but 'MyTerminal' at 10 px is wider than its tab. So the bar does not truncate: tabs.js::fitLabels measures every label against its own tab on the device, and if ANY label overflows the bar switches to compact mode (icons for all tabs, the label only under the active one). min_viewport_px is the width the tester holds the touch floor to.

shared_store._doc: #575 THE ONE on-phone repo store is cloud-drive's (ac_cloud-drive/build.json::storage.shared_root). `app` is that fleet application id (build.json::name), never a path: tools/resolve-targets.py reads the sibling app's declaration at build time and writes the root AND its git folder (storage.git_subdir, #606/#676 — the ONE place the store keeps clones) into src/cloud/targets.gen.json, and index.js composes every on-device git-tree path as <cordova externalRootDirectory>/<root>/<git_subdir>/<relative>. No device-absolute path is written here — the user id in it changes under a second profile — and this app clones NOTHING: the Backlog reads and writes the clone cloud-drive's git manager keeps there.

backlog._doc: Backlog reads the ONE existing source: the dist output of cloud-data-my-ai-memory/1.1.Product-Backlog (built by its own build.js). Nothing here re-derives it: `entry` is loaded and rendered as-is, and every other view is reached through the links that file itself carries ('Views: per project · per status …'). That repository is PRIVATE and this APK is PUBLIC, so the backlog is never baked into the bundle; it is read on the device from the clone cloud-drive keeps in the shared store (#575): source_dir is RELATIVE to the store's git folder (shared_root/git_subdir, #676). The tab lets the owner point it elsewhere (kept in localStorage), and its edit / folder actions open the same files in Acode's editor, so a change is written back into that clone for cloud-drive to commit and push.

agents._doc: The Agents tab reads the SAME source as Backlog (#562: 'they must read ONE source'): the backlog engine already derives task-effort, task-complexity and agent-model per task and curates agent-slot from assignments.json, and emits them as its own views — 'agent batches' (entry, below) and 'per agent-model', which the entry links to in its Views line. This tab renders `entry` through the very renderer Backlog uses, from backlog.source_dir; nothing about agents is derived here. SEAM: seams.js::listAgents is where the LIVE half (running status, token utilisation from the agent runner) plugs in; until then the tab shows its note under the view.

repos._doc: On-device directory whose children are listed as repositories (a child holding .git): the shared store's git folder itself (#575/#676: shared_root/git_subdir, where cloud-drive actually clones), so what cloud-drive cloned is what Repos lists. `root` is RELATIVE to that git folder ('' = the folder itself). SEAM: seams.js::listRepos is the stub a real provider (gitea / cloud-myterminal's workspace broker) replaces.

browser._doc: The Browser tab opens LOCAL pages in Acode's own in-app browser plugin (src/plugins/browser, the one Acode's Run command uses). `presets` are local servers the owner runs on the phone.

chat._doc: THE ONE DECLARATION of the Chat tab (replaced Home). The page is Cloud Search's chat (Chat > Search) without the search boxes: one message list, streamed replies, one composer. Everything fleet-shaped is DERIVED at build time by tools/resolve-targets.py into src/cloud/targets.gen.json: the agents (fleet_services, every service named agent_prefix*), the gateway URL (gateway.service's private_dns) and the fleet MCP servers (fleet_mcp, names only). What is declared here is only what the fleet data cannot say: the order the owner asked for (Hermes, OpenClaw first), what each backend accepts per request (model, effort, permission mode, MCP, functions), and the words.
chat._doc_fleet_services: The fleet's private service list as this repository carries it (cloud-c3 bakes it too). An agent is a service whose name starts with agent_prefix; its private_dns is where the mesh reaches it.
chat._doc_fleet_mcp: The derived .mcp.json (cloud-infra 1_cloud-configs/dist/mcp.json via 0_apps): the fallback MCP list for an agent whose backend publishes none. Only the server NAMES are copied; urls and headers stay out of the APK.

gateway._doc: my-ai-api (cloud-agi-goose, WireGuard-only) is the fleet's agent gateway: one OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions that picks the agent with the X-Agent-Mode header (goose | hermes | claude-cli), GET /health lists the agents it serves and its plugins, GET /v1/mcp/status its MCP servers, GET /v1/mcp/search?q= its tools, GET /sessions the cross-device sessions. Verified against cloud-u-containers user-ai_my-ai-api/src/code/server.mjs on 2026-10-10.

direct._doc: OpenRouter itself, with the token from Profile & Config (or the fleet Account's). Not an agent: a plain streamed chat with the model picked in the catalogue.
direct.label: OpenRouter

agents.label: Hermes

model._doc: the gateway answers hermes mode with ITS HERMES_MODEL; a model in the request is ignored, so the button shows that model and does not pick

effort._doc: the gateway spreads every extra body field into its OpenRouter call (server.mjs forward: {...extra}), so reasoning.effort reaches the model when that model reasons

permission._doc: Hermes' own approvals.mode is a container setting (off = auto); the gateway takes no per-request switch, so the mode is applied as the instruction below

agents._doc: Nous Hermes Agent. The cloud-agi-hermes container serves Telegram only (its API server is off, compose.nix), so the app reaches Hermes through the gateway's hermes mode.

agents.label: OpenClaw
agents._doc: Asked for by the owner. NOT in the fleet (no cloud-agi-openclaw service, no gateway mode): shown as not deployed and disabled, never faked. It lights up when the fleet declares the service and the gateway serves the mode.

agents.label: Goose

permission._doc: goose runs with no approval prompts in the gateway (operator, 2026-09-19)

agents._doc: Block's goose, the gateway's default agent (my-ai wraps goose).

agents.label: Claude

model._doc: claude-superset-api runs the subscription claude CLI: an Anthropic row of the catalogue is passed as the CLI id (anthropic/claude-opus-5.5 -> claude-opus-5-5); other providers cannot be picked

permission._doc: the CLI has --permission-mode, but claude-superset-api takes no per-request flag; applied as the instruction below

agents._doc: The claude CLI on the subscription (cloud-agi-claude), through the gateway's claude-cli mode.

chat._doc_agents: Listed first, in this order (the owner's: Hermes, OpenClaw, then the rest). Any OTHER fleet service named agent_prefix* is appended by the resolver as 'no app API yet' (disabled), so a new agent shows up without a code change. The direct OpenRouter backend comes last.

effort._doc: Low / Medium / High / Max, sent as OpenRouter's reasoning.effort (which accepts low, medium, high and max, verified 2026-10-10) when the backend passes it and the model reasons (its supported_parameters lists reasoning, read from direct.models_url once a day). Otherwise the control is disabled with the reason.

permission._doc: Auto / Accept / Plan, shown on the composer. No backend the app reaches takes a per-request approval switch today (see each agent's permission._doc), so via=prompt sends the mode as a system instruction; a backend with via=param would get it as that request field instead. The direct OpenRouter backend has no tools, so the control is hidden there.

modes.label: Accept Mode
modes.instruction: Permission mode: accept edits. You may create and edit files without asking. Ask before running commands that change anything outside the files (installs, deploys, pushes, deletions).

modes.label: Plan Mode
modes.instruction: Permission mode: plan. Do not change anything and do not run tools that write. Read what you need, then answer with a numbered plan and wait for approval.

catalogue._doc: The model picker is libs:model-catalogue (Cloud Search's catalogue, one implementation), narrowed to these sections by the lib's own filter.

functions.label: Gateway sessions
functions._doc: GET /sessions: the cross-device sessions (claude, goose); tap resumes one's tail into a new chat

functions.label: Search tools
functions._doc: GET /v1/mcp/search?q=: the MCP tools the agent can call

functions.label: Skills
functions.prompt: List the skills and toolsets you can use right now, one line each.

functions.label: Memory
functions.prompt: What do you remember about me and my current work? Read your memory first.

functions.label: Log Claude in (OAuth)
functions._doc: POST /auth/login/start on claude-superset-api returns the OAuth link; the code goes back to /auth/login/code

chat._doc_functions: The More sheet. 'gateway' = every agent served through the gateway. A toggle/select is shown only when the gateway's live /health.plugins lists its plugin (fetched each time the sheet opens); offline, the whole list falls back to this declaration, marked offline. kind: sessions/tools/info call the gateway route; toggle/select set a per-request header, persisted per agent; prompt sends the text as a message; login runs the Claude OAuth; client acts on the chat itself.

account._doc: Profile & Config > Account opens this fleet app (resolved like MyTerminal) and reads its OpenRouter key over libs:text-tools.

myterminal._doc: THE ONE PLACE the MyTerminal target is named (#562). It is a fleet application id, never a package: tools/resolve-targets.py reads the sibling app whose build.json::name equals it and derives the package (android.application_id) and the launcher activity (its manifest) into src/cloud/targets.gen.json at build time. #561 renamed cloud-ide to cloud-myterminal; if a later rename happens, this one value moves and the resolver fails the build loudly until it does.
